text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD
- Vienna's ATX blue-chip share index fell by 2.61 percent on Tuesday as Wall Street losses dragged Europe's bourses down.
- U.S. victims of the nazis are taking legal action against major European insurers, including Austria's Wiener Allianz and Anker Versicherung.
- Agricultural income fell to 158,000 schillings per family member in 1996 from 175,871 schillings in 1995.
- Austrian papermaker Leykam, a unit of Dutch KNP BT, is still searching for a strategic partner. Talks with possible candidates are taking longer than expected.
- Constantia's dividend remained unchanged at 33 schillings. Profits rose although turnover remained constant.
DIE PRESSE
- Subsidies for young entrepreneurs have been halved by the government as the programme starts.

- Erich Hampel, chief executive of privatisation candidate, postal savings bank PSK, is a likely candidate to become a board member of Creditanstalt. Former minister Rudolf Scholten could then either become his successor or the chief of new stock exchange company Bourse AG.

- The three bidders for Austria's salt monopoly Salinen AG - Raiffeisenlandesbank OOe with Hannes Androsch's investment group, agricultural group Agrana plus salt producer Suedsalz and French Salins du Midi - will now present their respective plans for the company's future.
- Aluminium maker Amag will buy a stake in Constantia, while it sells its stake in Teich to Constantia.
- South African Breweries have now received a formal refusal for its plans to take over brewer Brau Union, a unit of beverage group BBAG.

- Three investment offers for a new train tunnel through the Semmering mountain in eastern Austria have been made. However all three bidders demand a greater participation in the project by the state.
KURIER
- Social Democrat Parliamentary President Heinz Fischer has reaffirmed his party's "no" to membership of NATO for the time being.
- Spending by Austria's ailing health insurances were lower than expected due to reforms by the government.
- Raiffeisenbank plans to buy a stake in the Czech Republic's bankrupt Agrobanka.
- Austrian Airlines does not fear competition with the full liberalisation of the European market.
SALZBURGER NACHRICHTEN
- The provincial Hypo-Banks are having talks with possible common partners for a strategic repositioning. Talks on a closer link-up have been scrapped.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- Insulator Economos' restructuring will take longer than planned so that a dividend is only likely by 1999.
